messages:
maria (eng-platform): heads up — pushed the VPC isolation rule to ap-southeast this morning and our GPU node bootstrap is failing on keystore/KMS calls :warning:

maria (eng-platform): logs show repeated decrypt errors during init, nodes timeout provisioning after ~90s

maria (eng-platform): sample error: 
```
2024-11-12T09:12:03Z kubelet[1234]: keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: user not authorized for kms:Decrypt
    endpoint: vpce-0a1b2c3d.ap-southeast-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
    request_id: b3f1e8aa
```

tom (eng-infra): @maria thanks — looks like the VPC endpoint policy denies the role assumed by our bootstrapper. Did we lock down the privatelink policy to only some principals? :eyes:

maria (eng-platform): yes, turned policy to org-only principals to comply with the new isolation requirements. Probably missed the transient node role used by the GPU warmpool.

lee (eng-sre): confirm that this is blocking new GPU nodes only? Existing warm nodes keep serving?

maria (eng-platform): correct. Warm pool nodes that already had cached KEK work fine. New node init goes to KMS, gets denied, then fails bootstrap -> node terminates and we lose capacity.

sara (eng-security): we tightened the policy because of recent audit findings — can't just open it up globally. But we need a workaround that preserves auditability.

tom (eng-infra): quick mitigation options I can think of: 1) add the bootstrap role to the vpce policy (small exception), 2) add a conditional allowing the privatelink caller if request originates from our NAT/peering CIDR, 3) introduce a short-lived ephemeral signing token that the bootstrapper can use so KMS access isn't broadened.

sara (eng-security): option1 acceptable short-term if we log all key usage separately (we need per-request audit ids). Option3 preferable long-term. We also need to think about egress: the current audit shipper duplicates KMS metadata to S3 and doubles egress costs when we fall back to public KMS endpoints. Cost team will complain.

maria (eng-platform): cost note: when nodes fallback to public KMS endpoint we saw a 3x increase in egress + KMS request counts in last incident. That spiked billing in ap-southeast because cross-region replication triggered.

lee (eng-sre): proposal: revert the strict vpce policy for the bootstrap role only (canary 10% of warm pool launches), enable detailed key usage logging (separate log stream tagged "vpce-bootstrap-canary"), and deploy a keystore-proxy cache in the VPC that reduces KMS calls.

maria (eng-platform): would the proxy require HSM access? or can it cache wrapped keys and serve short-term plaintext only to bootstrapper?

sara (eng-security): proxy must never serve plaintext long-term. We can cache wrapped keys (KEK-wrapped) and unwrap only inside an HSM-backed process. If that's heavy, we can at least cache KMS responses for 5m to reduce volume. Compliance ok with cached wrapped blobs if unwrap audit recorded.

tom (eng-infra): quick patch I can do today: add sts:AssumeRole principal for "gpu-bootstrapper" to the vpce policy and gate it behind a condition aws:SourceVpc == vpc-0deadbeef. That avoids opening it org-wide.

sara (eng-security): good. Also add an explicit condition requiring aws:RequestTag/audit-id so we can tie each decrypt to a trace id.

maria (eng-platform): i'll add the audit-id header in the bootstrapper and instrument the console to show counts. lee will you run the canary and watch capacity?

lee (eng-sre): yes. plan: staging patch now, production canary at 10% for 30m, then 50% for 1h, rollback if any additional failures or KMS error rate > 0.5%. I'll also watch node churn and autoscaler backoff metrics.

devops-bot: deploy job started: infra/vpce-policy/ap-southeast patch by tom — job 7892

tom (eng-infra): patch applied to staging. netstat+curl check to vpce ok: `curl https://vpce-0a1b2c3d.ap-southeast-1.vpce.amazonaws.com/health` -> 200

maria (eng-platform): staging warm pool now provisioning new GPU nodes successfully. No decrypt errors in last 12m.

sara (eng-security): filing compliance ticket: COMP-2024-314 — documents exception with audit steps and retention. We need SOC-2 proof that we scoped the exception and that logs are immutable.

lee (eng-sre): starting prod canary now (10% warp launches). Monitoring dashboard: kube_autoscaler.backoff = 0, node_init.fail_rate = 0.02 -> looking good so far.

maria (eng-platform): cost owners FYI — this exception may add small KMS request delta; estimate <2% monthly uplift if we keep it under conditions.

sara (eng-security): timeline: short-term exception for bootstrap role, medium-term implement keystore-proxy with cached wrapped blobs, long-term move to ephemeral hardware-backed tokens and reduce direct KMS calls during init.

tom (eng-infra): action items:
- (tom) add vpce policy exception for gpu-bootstrapper (done, staged -> prod canary)
- (maria) add audit-id tagging to bootstrapper requests (in progress)
- (lee) run canary and report metrics (in progress)
- (sara) create compliance ticket and retention proof (done)

maria (eng-platform): if canary stays green for 2 hours we'll promote and close the incident. If not, fallback is to route new provisioning to dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 for critical jobs only.

lee (eng-sre): will post a short follow-up in #incidents with numbers. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
